transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just can't get past how rough and worn my face and hands look these days. It's really getting to me. 

Whenever I have to go into town and deal with a banker or some county person, I just feel like they're staring right at the cracks and the spots, all the sagging skin. My wife tells me I just look like a man who's worked outdoors his whole life, which I have, but... I just can't stop focusing on how bad it looks.
How much time do you find yourself spending thinking about the way your skin looks, and does it interfere with your daily life?

Well, I guess I think about it a fair amount. It's hard to put an exact number of hours on it, but it's on my mind most days. And, yeah, it does get in the way. I've actually missed some important calls with the bank, and I've put off making decisions about the farm because I just couldn't get myself looking... acceptable enough to sit down in a room with people. My wife and I run a little retreat and sell some crafts, and I've stopped agreeing to be in any of the photos we use to promote it. I just don't want people seeing me looking like this.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, trying to cover up certain parts of your skin, or comparing yourself to others, because of how you feel about your appearance?

Yeah, I do. Before I have to head out for something important, like a loan meeting or setting up our table at a craft fair, I end up checking the bathroom mirror over and over. Then I get out to the truck and I'm checking the rearview mirror, too. I'll sit there turning my hat this way and that, trying to see if pulling it down lower hides the lines around my eyes or the spots on my forehead. 

And I definitely compare myself. When we have younger guys out helping on the farm, I catch myself looking at their hands, and then looking at mine, just seeing how smooth theirs are compared to how cracked and worn mine look. By the time I'm done doing all that checking and comparing, I've usually wasted a good chunk of time that I really should have been using to get work done around the farm.
How much do these concerns about your appearance upset you or make it hard for you to do the things you need or want to do?

Well, it upsets me quite a bit, honestly. Like I mentioned before, it really does make it hard to get things done. I've missed important calls with the bankers, and I've put off making decisions about the farm just because I couldn't get myself looking... acceptable enough to go sit down in a room with people. And it hurts our business, too. My wife and I run that little retreat and sell our crafts, and I've completely stopped agreeing to be in any of the photos we use to promote it. I just can't stand the thought of folks seeing my face and hands looking so worn out. So, yeah, it definitely gets in the way of what I need to be doing.

When you look in the mirror and see these lines, spots, and roughness on your face and hands, do you feel that these are things that other people would notice and judge you for, or do you feel that you're noticing flaws that most people wouldn't even see?

Well, I definitely feel like other people notice it. That's really what brings me in here, to be honest. I just can't get past how rough and worn my face and hands look. It feels like... well, like every banker or county person I have to deal with is just staring right at the cracks, the spots, and the sagging. 

Now, my wife, she tells me I'm making a big deal out of nothing. She says I just look like a normal man who's worked outdoors his whole life and that nobody else is paying attention to it. But I just don't see it that way. I really feel like people are looking right at those flaws and judging me for them.

When you're worried about how your face and hands look, do you feel that the flaws you're seeing are very noticeable and unusual, or do you think they might be minor things that most people wouldn't really pay attention to?

Like I was just saying, I really do feel like they're very noticeable. Honestly, that's exactly what brings me in to see you. I just... I can't get past how rough and worn my face and hands look. To me, they don't seem like minor things at all. 

It feels like every banker or county person I sit down with is just staring right at the cracks, the spots, and the sagging skin. Now, my wife, she swears they're minor. She keeps telling me I just look like a normal man who's worked outdoors his whole life and that nobody else cares. But I just can't see it that way. To me, they stand out like a sore thumb.
When you feel upset about your appearance, is it mainly about your face and hands, or do you worry about other parts of your body as well?

It's really just my face and hands. I mean, I don't really think about the rest of my body. It's just... those are the parts that are out there for everyone to see, you know? The parts that aren't covered up by clothes. So, no, I don't really worry about anything else, just the face and the hands.

When you're in a situation like a loan meeting or a craft fair, and you're worried about people noticing your face and hands, is your main concern that they will think less of you because of how you look, or is it more about being embarrassed or judged in general, even if you're not sure exactly what others might be thinking?

I'm not really sure how to separate those two things, to be honest. I guess... I haven't really thought about exactly what words are going through their heads. 

I just know I feel embarrassed when I'm sitting there across from them. It just feels like they're judging me for how worn out and rough I look. Whether they're specifically thinking less of me or just staring... I don't know for sure. I just know it makes me really uncomfortable, and I just want to hide my hands under the table.

When you worry about the way your face and hands look, do you feel that the flaws you’re noticing are ones that others could clearly see and would agree are significant, or do you think they might be things that only you notice or see as important?

Well, I guess I'm not entirely sure. Like I said before, my wife tells me nobody else notices or cares, and that I just look like a guy who works outside. So maybe they don't see it as being as bad as I do. But when I'm looking in the mirror, or when I'm sitting across from someone, it just feels so obvious to me. I can't really say for certain if they agree with me or if it's just me... I just know how it feels on my end.

When you look at your face and hands and see these flaws, do you feel that they are actually physically worse than they really are, or do you believe that what you see is an accurate reflection of how they truly look?

I don't really know. I mean, to me, it's just what I see. I look at my hands, I look in the mirror, and that's just... that's what's there. I don't know if I'm making it out to be worse than it is. I just know it looks bad to me, and it bothers me. I guess I can't really tell if my mind is playing tricks on me or if it's just the truth of how I look.

When you see these flaws on your face and hands, do you believe that they are clearly visible and objectively significant, or do you ever wonder if you're focusing on things that most people wouldn't even notice?

Well, I guess I do wonder about it sometimes. Mostly because my wife keeps telling me nobody else cares. So maybe I am just focusing on things other folks wouldn't pay much mind to. 

But... when I look right at them, they seem pretty clear to me. I can't really tell you for sure if they're objectively significant, as you put it, or if it's just me zeroing in on them. I just don't really know. I only know that they stand out to me when I look.
Have there been times when you avoided going out altogether or refused to participate in important events because of how your face and hands look?

Yeah, there have been. I mean... I've actually missed some calls with our bankers over it, and I've put off some pretty important farm decisions just because I couldn't get myself looking acceptable enough to go sit down with people. 

And we run a little retreat and do some craft sales, but I've completely stopped agreeing to take any photos that would help promote it. I just can't put myself out there like that when I look this way. So, yeah, it definitely gets in the way of things I need to be doing.

When you look at your face and hands, do you feel certain that the flaws you see are physically real and objectively noticeable, or do you sometimes think that what you're seeing might not be as others see it?

Well, I feel like we just touched on this a minute ago, but... no, I guess I'm not completely certain. 

When I look at myself, the flaws are very real to me. They're right there. But like I was saying about my wife, she tells me people don't see it. So I do sometimes think that maybe other folks aren't seeing it the exact same way I am. I just can't say for sure either way.
Would you say that the way you see your face and hands is significantly worse than what someone else looking at you would actually notice?

Doc, I feel like we're kind of beating a dead horse here. I really don't know how to answer that any differently than I just did. 

I can't look through somebody else's eyes. If my wife is right, then I guess... yeah, maybe I do see it as worse than what someone else would actually notice. But I just don't know for sure. I can't speak for what other people are seeing. I only know that when I look at my hands and my face, it looks terrible to me.
